dedupe_keys.name: hy2dl deep learning rainfall runoff library

description: Hy2DL is a Python library for building deep-learning rainfall-runoff models. Its maintainers provide implementations and examples that work with large-sample hydrology collections including CAMELS-GB, CAMELS-US, CAMELS-DE, CAMELS-CH and Caravan. Users obtain a dataset separately, configure meteorological and basin attributes, and train or run a neural model; outputs are predicted streamflow and benchmark results for the configured catchments and period. Spatial and temporal coverage follow the external training data, not a bundled global watershed map. BSD-3-Clause source, a PyPI package, configuration examples and documentation are public. The README explicitly says users must download datasets independently. Predictive skill may shift outside the training basins and climate regimes, so an untested local hydrograph should not be treated as calibrated flood evidence. It supports runoff forecasting and comparison with physical catchment models. The catalogue's model-raven is one separate hydrological framework for comparison; no coupling was tested. The earlier KIT-HYD repository points to this maintained home. No training data or package was downloaded.
